content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge resolves a challenge involving the challenger's own footed chain by pointing to Matthew 1:20's own words, so K-C's chain-vs-chain requirement governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse: one reading forbids deciding the collision by the single linked verse's own positive wording against the challenger's footed chain; the other reading forbids only the retired absence-of-contrary-in-own-words test.","why":"The judge notes the challenger's analogy is footed but then resolves the collision by the sentence's own words, i.e., verse by verse rather than chain against chain by footing."}
